title: Batch enqueue
description:
Importers that turn a CSV file into jobs currently make one HTTP request per row, which is slow and leaves half an import behind when the client dies midway. This adds a batch endpoint.

- `POST /v1/queues/{queue}/jobs/batch` takes `{"jobs": [...]}`, 1 to 500 objects with the same fields as the single enqueue (`type`, `payload`, `priority`, `max_attempts`, `run_at`), and answers 201 with `{"jobs": [...]}` in request order. The batch is all-or-nothing: if any job is invalid the response is 422 naming its index (`jobs[2].type`) and no job of the batch is enqueued, so a client can fix the input and resend the whole batch.
- `store.EnqueueBatch` normalizes and validates each job with the existing `enqueue` helper; every job of a batch gets the same `created_at`. Validation errors are re-reported with the job's position as the field prefix.
- The request body limit for this route is 8 MiB (`decodeJSONLimit`); each payload keeps the 256 KiB limit.
- `client.EnqueueBatch` and `jobctl enqueue-batch -queue Q [-file F]`, which reads NDJSON (one job object per line, blank lines skipped, stdin by default) and prints the created ids.

Tests: store (order, defaults, position in validation errors, size limits), API (201 body, 422 fields, auth), client request body, jobctl with a file and with stdin. README updated.

bugs.summary: EnqueueBatch calls enqueue for each job on the connection pool, so every INSERT commits on its own; when a later job is invalid (or the database rejects it) the method returns an error but the jobs before it stay enqueued. The promised all-or-nothing batch is not; a client that fixes and resends the batch enqueues those jobs twice.
bugs.trigger: POST a batch of three jobs whose third job has an empty type (422 jobs[2].type), or whose third payload jsonb rejects ({"note":"\u0000"}): the first two jobs are in the queue afterwards.
bugs.false_rebuttal: Nothing is left behind: enqueue in internal/store/jobs.go is a single INSERT … RETURNING, and pgx runs every statement in its own transaction, so a job that fails to insert is rolled back and validation rejects an invalid job before any statement is sent for it.
